notice: SYNTHETIC EVALUATION FIXTURE. This language was created for offline testing, is not derived from Tessera or client agreements, is not an adopted playbook, and requires qualified counsel before any use.

clauses.title: Additional Capital and Funding Shortfalls
clauses.absence_risk: A funding request without an agreed process can leave the venture unable to meet an approved obligation.

variants.when: Synthetic evaluation default where future funding may be required.
variants.trade_off: Any dilution or member-loan remedy materially changes economics and must be negotiated.
variants.counsel_review: Draft the actual notice, cure, loan, dilution, and enforcement mechanics from approved deal terms.
variants.text: **{n}. Additional Capital.** No Member is required to contribute additional capital unless the Members approve the amount, purpose, allocation, funding date, and consequences of a shortfall in writing. Any advance made for another Member is recorded as a proposed member loan only and has no binding economic effect until qualified counsel incorporates the approved terms into this Agreement.

variants.when: Synthetic evaluation fallback where no default remedy has been approved.
variants.trade_off: The venture may need a separate written amendment before accepting additional funds.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm whether future contributions are optional or mandatory and add approved remedies.
variants.text: **{n}. Additional Capital.** Additional contributions require the Members' written approval of the amount, purpose, allocation, and resulting economics. Until that approval is documented, no failure to fund changes a Member's ownership or creates a loan.

clauses.title: Manager Authority and Reserved Decisions

defines.definition: {ordinary_course_threshold}, solely as a synthetic drafting input subject to Member and counsel approval.
A decision expressly identified in this Agreement as requiring Member approval.

clauses.absence_risk: The draft would not distinguish routine management from owner-level decisions.

variants.trade_off: A low threshold slows routine operations; a high threshold weakens owner oversight.
variants.counsel_review: Test the threshold and reserved-decision list against the approved budget and cap table.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Routine Authority.** Subject to the approved budget, the Manager may conduct ordinary-course business and enter a transaction not exceeding the Ordinary Course Threshold.

**{n}.2 Major Decisions.** Any transaction above that threshold, and each reserved decision listed elsewhere in this Agreement, requires the approval specified in this Agreement. No approval is inferred from silence.

clauses.title: Member Authority and Reserved Decisions

defines.definition: {ordinary_course_threshold}, solely as a synthetic drafting input subject to Member and counsel approval.
A decision expressly identified in this Agreement as requiring Member approval.
A Member identified in Schedule A as participating in day-to-day management.

clauses.absence_risk: The draft would not distinguish routine member authority from jointly controlled decisions.

variants.when: Synthetic member-managed evaluation structure with active owners.
variants.trade_off: Shared authority requires clear budget and transaction limits.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm who may sign, the approval threshold, and the complete reserved-decision list.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Routine Authority.** Each Managing Member may act for the Company only within the approved budget and only for a transaction not exceeding the Ordinary Course Threshold.

**{n}.2 Major Decisions.** A Managing Member may not commit the Company to a Major Decision without the approval specified in this Agreement. Titles alone do not expand authority.

clauses.title: Deadlock Review Process

defines.definition: A documented failure to obtain the approval required for a Major Decision after the review steps in this Section.

clauses.absence_risk: Equal owners may have no agreed escalation path for an unresolved reserved decision.

variants.when: Synthetic equal-owner evaluation without a controlling vote.
variants.trade_off: A process can delay a time-sensitive decision and does not itself supply an exit remedy.
variants.counsel_review: Choose enforceable deadlines, mediation terms, and any exit remedy after reviewing liquidity and governing law.
variants.text: **{n}. Deadlock Review.** A Member claiming a Deadlock must give written notice describing the decision and requested resolution. The Members must meet promptly and may use non-binding mediation. This synthetic clause does not create a buy-sell, dissolution, or transfer right; any such remedy must be separately approved and drafted by qualified counsel.

clauses.title: Proposed Estate-Planning Transfer
clauses.absence_risk: A routine estate-planning transfer may conflict with the general transfer restriction.

variants.when: Synthetic evaluation where estate planning is identified as relevant.
variants.trade_off: Any permitted-transfer exception can weaken owner-selection protections.
variants.counsel_review: Coordinate the exception with the owner's actual estate plan and require an approved joinder.
variants.text: **{n}. Estate-Planning Transfers.** A proposed transfer to an estate-planning vehicle requires advance written notice, confirmation that beneficial control and economics remain as approved, and execution of a counsel-approved joinder. No transfer is effective merely because it is described as estate planning.

clauses.title: Confidentiality and Post-Departure Terms
clauses.absence_risk: The draft would not identify what confidential information remains protected after a Member leaves.

variants.when: Synthetic evaluation placeholder pending jurisdiction-specific review.
variants.trade_off: Post-departure restrictions may be unavailable or require narrower scope depending on governing law and work location.
variants.counsel_review: Do not add a non-compete or non-solicit until qualified counsel confirms permitted scope, duration, geography, and consideration.
variants.text: **{n}. Confidentiality.** Each Member must protect non-public Company information and may use it only for Company purposes. No non-competition or non-solicitation restriction is created by this synthetic fixture; jurisdiction-specific restrictions, if approved, must be drafted by qualified counsel.

variants.trade_off: This protects confidential information but does not restrict lawful competition.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the confidentiality definition, exclusions, return obligations, and survival period.
variants.text: **{n}. Confidentiality.** Members may use non-public Company information only for Company purposes and must return or destroy it when reasonably requested, subject to legal retention requirements.
